title: Mohammed Shami retires from Tests with 229 wickets, 13 years to the day after Eden debut
dek: The Bengal fast bowler, 36, thanked the BCCI and the Cricket Association of Bengal and will keep playing white-ball cricket and the IPL.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Mohammed Shami, the Bengal fast bowler who took 229 wickets in 64 Tests for India, has retired from Test cricket, 13 years to the day after his debut at Eden Gardens. He will keep playing white-ball cricket, including the IPL and domestic matches.

Shami, 36, announced the decision on Friday in a video posted on Instagram, holding his Test cap, number 279, and a red ball. "Today I am deciding to retire from Test cricket with a heavy heart and unlimited beautiful memories," he wrote, according to reports. He thanked the Board of Control for Cricket in India and the Cricket Association of Bengal, his home association, for backing him early in his career, and ended: "Thank you, Test Cricket."

## A career in numbers

Shami made his Test debut against West Indies at Eden Gardens on 6 November 2013, taking 4 for 71 and 5 for 47 as India won by an innings and 51 runs. He went on to take 229 wickets at an average of 27.71 and an economy rate of 3.30, with six five-wicket hauls and 12 four-wicket hauls. His best figures were 6 for 56.

He was at his most dangerous away from home. He took 131 wickets in 35 Tests in India, South Africa and the West Indies at an average below 25, according to one analysis, including 5 for 28 in the second innings at Johannesburg in 2018. At Lord's in August 2021 he also made an unbeaten 56 off 70 balls, sharing an 89-run ninth-wicket stand with Jasprit Bumrah that set up an Indian win.

His last Test was the World Test Championship final against Australia at The Oval in June 2023, which India lost by 209 runs. Injuries then kept him out of the Test side, and he has not played for India since the 2025 Champions Trophy.

## Still bowling for Bengal

Shami has continued to play first-class cricket for Bengal. In Bengal's Ranji Trophy match against Maharashtra at Eden Gardens, which ended on Thursday, he took 4 for 37 in Maharashtra's first innings, though Bengal lost by 10 wickets. In his video he said he would play domestic cricket "if required for fitness" and would "definitely continue playing white-ball cricket, whether it is IPL or domestic matches", according to reports.

He was also the leading wicket-taker at the 2023 ODI World Cup, with 24 wickets in seven innings. Born in Uttar Pradesh, he moved to Kolkata as a teenager to play club cricket and built his career in Bengal's domestic system.

## What happens next

Shami's retirement leaves him available for one-day, Twenty20 and IPL cricket. He did not say whether he would keep playing Ranji Trophy matches for Bengal this season beyond what he needs for fitness. Neither the BCCI nor the Cricket Association of Bengal had issued a statement on his retirement by Saturday morning.
